title: Service Requests and Service Call Fees under Homeowner Service Contracts
content:
## Placing a service request

A service request under a Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contract covers one failed item serviced by one trade; a failure that needs two trades is placed as two requests, each carrying its own fee. Service requests are accepted only while the contract status is active (read from the contract record).

## Fees by request type

| Request | Fee posted |
|---|---|
| New failure | the contract's service call fee, once |
| Recall within the guarantee window (same covered item as an earlier authorization on the contract) | no fee |
| Return visit placed after the guarantee window | it is a new-failure request and carries the fee |
| Second opinion | the contract's service call fee multiplied by the tier's second-opinion fee rate, rounded to the cent; when that amount is zero no fee is posted |
| Routine request for which the customer asks for an after-hours visit | also the tier's after-hours surcharge on a non-emergency request; nothing is posted when the tier's surcharge is zero |
| Emergency request | never the after-hours surcharge |

**Recall window.** A recall request is charged no fee when it concerns the same covered item as an earlier authorization on the contract and is placed no later than the tier's repair guarantee (calendar days) after that earlier repair is completed (the replacement labor guarantee for a Bridgewell-provided replacement); the count starts the day after the completion date and the boundary day itself qualifies. The completion date and the authorization are read from the claim-handling record named by the recall.

*Boundary pair, hypothetical, repair guarantee of 30 days, repair completed June 1:* a recall placed July 1 (day 30) carries no fee; a return visit placed July 2 (day 31) is a new-failure request and carries the fee.

**Second opinion.** A second-opinion request may be placed only after an initial determination on the same item. *Hypothetical:* a 125.00 service call fee with a rate of 1.00 gives a 125.00 second-opinion fee; with a rate of 0.00 the amount is zero and no fee is posted.

## Emergency or routine

A request is an emergency when the failure leaves the home without heat while the outdoor temperature is below 40°F, without cooling while it is above 90°F, without running water, or without electrical power, or causes an active water leak that cannot be stopped at a fixture shutoff; every other request is routine.

## Once per type; refunds

The fee of each fee type is charged at most once per service request. When the tier's fee-refund-before-dispatch setting is Yes and the customer cancels the request before any contractor dispatch is recorded for it, the fees collected on that request are refunded in full.

> Fees are not refunded because a failure is determined not covered, because the customer declines a covered repair or replacement, or because the customer accepts cash in lieu.
>
> **Retirement notice:** this sentence is no longer in force for (a) a customer-elected cash settlement on a request whose repair authorization stalled and was reversed, as to the standard visit fee collected on that request, and (b) the acceptance of a company-elected cash offer on a recall of earlier Bridgewell work, as to the standard visit fee paid for that earlier work. Those fees are settled under the current rules for those settlements. For every other fee the sentence remains the rule.

A fee collected in error, such as a standard fee on a qualifying recall, is refunded with the refund reason "charged in error".

superseded_clauses: Fees are not refunded because a failure is determined not covered, because the customer declines a covered repair or replacement, or because the customer accepts cash in lieu.
